h2: Eddy current testing in Houston: exchanger bundles, power plant condensers and coated welds
html:
Eddy current testing in Houston: exchanger bundles, power plant condensers and coated welds

In Houston, eddy current testing is mostly tube inspection. It covers exchanger bundles in the ship channel refineries and chemical plants, and condensers and feedwater heaters in the region's power stations. Surface eddy current and ACFM also find weld cracks on marine and offshore steel without removing the coating. Atlantis, headquartered in Houston, brings ET crews and probe sets for each turnaround or outage.

Refinery and chemical exchanger work. A large ship channel refinery, such as ExxonMobil's 588,000 barrel-a-day Baytown plant or Pemex's Deer Park refinery, pulls many bundles in each turnaround. Tube inspection is often on the critical path. Bobbin probes screen copper alloy, stainless and titanium tubes for pitting, baffle wear and general thinning. Array or motorized rotating probes then characterize the tubes that will be plugged or decide whether a bundle is retubed. The plant's inspection group sets the plugging criteria. The ET report has to show the tube map, the calibration standard and the probe fill factor, so the plugging decision can be traced back to the data.

Carbon steel bundles and fin-fans. Many Gulf Coast plants use carbon steel exchanger tubes and air-cooled fin-fan units. Conventional eddy current is weak on ferromagnetic tubing, so those are usually scoped for IRIS. Each bundle's method is settled from the tube material list before the turnaround starts, not on the day the bundle is pulled.

Power station condensers. NRG's W.A. Parish Generating Station, near Thompsons in Fort Bend County, has about 3,650 MW of coal and gas units and is one of the largest conventional power plants in the country. Other stations around Houston add more condensers and feedwater heaters. Their tubes are screened with eddy current during planned outages, which Texas generators usually schedule away from the summer peak. A full-bundle survey trended against earlier campaigns shows whether tube damage is accelerating.

Coated welds on marine and offshore steel. Houston-managed offshore topsides, crane pedestals and ship channel dock structures have weld toes that need crack checks under the paint. Weld-probe eddy current and ACFM inspection find surface-breaking cracks through coatings, so the steel is not left bare in humid Gulf air.

  • Non-ferrous exchanger tubes: bobbin screening, array or rotating-probe sizing
  • Carbon steel and fin-fan tubing: IRIS instead of conventional eddy current
  • Condensers and feedwater heaters: outage campaigns trended year on year
  • Coated weld toes: crack detection without coating removal

Where to go. The national service is set out on eddy current testing. Turnaround scopes are planned through turnaround and shutdown inspection, and plant-specific context is on power generation NDT in Houston and inspection services in Houston. Tube inspection results can be issued as signed reports through the ERP reports app. For ET technician training, see eddy current training. Send the bundle list and tube materials through the Houston ET enquiry.
